reading: SPARK is a Bellingham nonprofit museum devoted to the history of electrical invention and accessible, inspirational science education. It connects rare historical artifacts and the long thread of discovery to live demonstrations, school field trips, knowledgeable guides, hands-on STEM kits and a planned interactive Wonderlab. Its vocabulary is curiosity, discovery, invention, exhibits, demonstrations, voltage and wonder; its tone is playful, theatrical and family-oriented. Its distinctive character comes from putting old technologies such as crystal radios, electric lamps and image projection alongside a spectacular live electrical show, while treating the museum as part of a local community of educators, volunteers and neighboring places. The crawl also contains event listings, archive and tag pages, and visitor and support information; many repeat the same material or offer only short excerpts.

enemies.idea: The Voltage Ringmaster builds a cage of crawling arcs around anyone who watches its demonstration, demanding a bigger reaction before it opens the circuit.
enemies.why: A spectacle becomes a timing puzzle: avert your eyes to weaken it, but watch the arcs to find a way out.

enemies.idea: The Living Timeline joins early electrical artifacts into a long mechanical centipede, adding every tool it catches as the next link in its supposed history of invention.
enemies.why: The crew can interrupt its chain by separating mismatched eras instead of simply attacking its armored head.

enemies.idea: A candle-and-mirror projectionist casts giant moving shadows that detach from their owners and try to herd them into the beam.
enemies.why: Moving the modest light source changes the battlefield and can turn the shadows against their maker.

enemies.idea: A reel-life hunter advances one frame whenever the lights flicker, splicing the crew's last few movements into a loop it can replay.
enemies.why: The crew can break its rhythm by interrupting the projection or deliberately feeding it a useless loop.

enemies.idea: An arc-lamp scavenger wears a blinding factory lamp and searches for anything it can add to its circuit, plunging the room into darkness between bursts.
enemies.why: Its light both reveals its position and makes it dangerous to face; darkness becomes useful cover.

enemies.idea: An electrified glass menagerie lures curious visitors with beautiful glowing shapes, then rearranges its fragile tubes into a crackling maze.
enemies.why: The prettiest route is often the trap, and careful handling can open safe paths without smashing the display.

enemies.idea: A crystal-radio whisperer gathers faint signals from the room and rebroadcasts misleading calls for help through a forest of mineral antennae.
enemies.why: The crew must locate the real signal by moving and listening, while the enemy gives away its position whenever it transmits.

enemies.idea: A theremin sentinel senses approaching hands and answers each gesture with a note that steers nearby swarm machines toward the performer.
enemies.why: A fight becomes a silent dance: stillness hides the crew, while deliberate gestures can conduct the machines elsewhere.

enemies.idea: A sewing-machine crawler stitches loose cables, coats and doors together into one enormous seam, trapping whoever tries to cross it.
enemies.why: Pulling the right thread can unravel an entire barrier, but the wrong one tightens it.

enemies.idea: A vacuum pump insists that every occupied room must be emptied, rolling in with clattering valves and dragging loose equipment toward its intake.
enemies.why: Its suction can be redirected to pull obstacles or other swarm machines off balance.

enemies.idea: A cathode-ray inspector hunts by the glow of its screen, searching for hidden mechanisms inside the crew's equipment and prying those pieces loose.
enemies.why: Solid cover is unreliable, but an interposed decoy can make the inspector dismantle the wrong object.

enemies.idea: A snap-together circuit swarm keeps rebuilding itself into new machines, stealing conductive objects to complete whichever shape it needs next.
enemies.why: Each stolen component telegraphs its next form, giving the crew a chance to replace a piece and change the circuit.

enemies.idea: A discovery-station mimic offers an inviting hands-on puzzle; each successful connection powers another limb of the machine hiding underneath.
enemies.why: The crew can solve the exhibit backward, diverting its energy while it expects another enthusiastic experiment.

enemies.idea: A tour marshal divides the crew into large assembly and small gallery groups, then seals different routes behind them to keep its tour on schedule.
enemies.why: Separated players get different clues and must reunite by coordinating across the partition.

enemies.idea: A mechanical docent tells an endless story about every object it sees, pinning listeners in place with spotlights whenever they interrupt.
enemies.why: The crew can ask a question or introduce a strange object to send its attention wandering.

enemies.idea: An overdecorated mad-science patrol treats every encounter as a demonstration, setting up elaborate apparatus before it attacks.
enemies.why: Its conspicuous preparations give the crew time to sabotage the punchline or turn the apparatus around.

enemies.idea: A materials shaper harvests bone-like needles and wooden handles from its surroundings to make crude but constantly changing tools for the swarm.
enemies.why: The danger evolves visibly from whatever materials are nearby, inviting the crew to control what it can reach.

enemies.idea: A perpetual-motion claimant spins faster whenever anyone tries to stop it, quietly stealing power from neighboring exhibits to keep its boast alive.
enemies.why: Finding and disconnecting its hidden supply exposes the trick and ends the chase.

enemies.idea: A performance-center stage rig lowers curtains and raises platforms around the crew, forcing them to hit marks for a demonstration that never ends.
enemies.why: The changing stage offers moving cover and high routes to reach the machinery above.

enemies.idea: A holiday marvel collector strings early electric lights across the room, connecting every captured object into a glittering but unstable decoration.
enemies.why: One carefully interrupted connection can darken a whole strand and free its prizes.

enemies.idea: The haunted-lab gamekeeper challenges intruders to interactive experiments and converts each unfinished game into a little mechanical pursuer.
enemies.why: Finishing or cleverly redirecting a game prevents another pursuer from joining the chase.

enemies.idea: A home-entertainment assembler piles screens and speakers into a rolling fortress, drowning out real sounds with a carefully synchronized fake scene.
enemies.why: The crew can spot the mismatch between image and sound, then use it to slip past its attention.

allies.idea: A surviving volunteer guide knows which old demonstrations can safely interrupt a swarm circuit and points the crew toward useful artifacts.
allies.why: Local knowledge gives the crew options without solving the problem for them.

allies.idea: A stubborn discovery station still invites experimentation; rearranging its pieces produces a temporary safe circuit that opens a path.
allies.why: The museum's hands-on curiosity becomes a practical way to fight back.

allies.idea: An uncorrupted crystal receiver picks up faint calls from isolated survivors without announcing their location to the swarm.
allies.why: Listening and positioning can uncover routes and rescue opportunities.

allies.idea: A resourceful educator carries a small checkout kit of circuit pieces and helps the crew improvise switches from what they find.
allies.why: Simple components reward creative combinations and make the crew active collaborators.

allies.idea: A live-show guide remembers the timing of the electrical demonstrations and can warn the crew when the next arc is about to leap.
allies.why: A dramatic performance skill becomes a reliable rhythm for crossing a dangerous room.

bosses.idea: The Grand Demonstrator has assembled the collection into a giant staged history of electricity. Each phase recruits a different invention, while its central conductor demands the audience stay for one final, ever-larger demonstration.
bosses.why: The whole museum becomes a sequence of recognizable mechanisms; breaking the links between them dismantles the spectacle piece by piece.

bosses.idea: The Curiosity Engine has taken over the interactive gallery and decided that every question must produce a new machine. It captures the crew's experiments, builds a swarm answer, and grows stronger whenever the same solution is repeated.
bosses.why: The boss turns the museum's love of discovery into an escalating challenge that rewards trying a different idea each round.

bosses.idea: The Million-Volt Master of Ceremonies conducts an unending live show, using projection, shadow and arcing machinery to turn the entire performance space into its circuit.
bosses.why: The crew can change the show's timing and redirect its spectacle, making the room itself the instrument of victory.

events.idea: A projector is showing a shadow of the crew several seconds before they move. Its beam also reveals a safe route past a dormant machine, but only while someone keeps the candle steady.
events.why: One person must maintain the light while the others decide whether to trust what they see.

events.idea: A crate of STEM kit pieces has spilled across the floor. A tiny swarm machine is trying to complete a circuit with them before the crew can build a switch to open a nearby door.
events.why: Both sides race for the same simple parts, with several possible arrangements.

events.idea: A crystal radio alternates between a genuine faint message and the swarm's imitation. Shifting its position makes one clearer and the other fade.
events.why: A quiet listening challenge rewards patience and movement.

events.idea: A sewing crawler has accidentally stitched a useful supply bag to a curtain that is slowly rising into the rafters.
events.why: The crew must choose whether to climb, cut the seam, or stop the mechanism before the bag vanishes.

events.idea: A live electrical demonstration restarts on its own; its arcs briefly illuminate footprints leading through an otherwise dark room.
events.why: The hazard also supplies the information needed to cross it.

events.idea: A self-guided discovery station has two sockets: one powers a safe exit light, while the other wakes a dormant swarm component. The labels have been switched.
events.why: The crew can trace the wiring or take a calculated chance rather than rely on labels.

events.idea: A guide's tour route has been divided by a locked partition. Clues to the release are distributed between the large-group assembly area and the small-group gallery.
events.why: Separated crew members have to describe what they see and put the two halves together.

events.idea: A glowing glass display casts a beautiful pattern on the wall. Moving its tubes changes the pattern and reveals a concealed passage, but the tubes are fragile.
events.why: Care and observation turn an alluring exhibit into a tactile puzzle.

events.idea: A runaway pump tugs loose notes and tools toward its intake. Among the fluttering papers is a diagram someone needs to retrieve.
events.why: The crew can block, redirect or ride the airflow, each with a different risk to the diagram.

events.idea: An abandoned haunted-lab game still offers a prize: a small working component. Its mechanical opponent will surrender it if the crew can complete the experiment first.
events.why: A brief contest supplies a useful reward without requiring a fight.

events.idea: A stage platform rises whenever the crew makes noise. A needed control is overhead, but too much noise lifts the platform into a nest of machines.
events.why: The crew must meter its own movement and sound to stop at the right height.

events.idea: A string of old holiday lights leads through a doorway and into a pile of swarm parts. One bulb is dark, leaving the circuit harmless until something bridges the gap.
events.why: The crew can preserve the gap for safe passage or close it to power a distraction.

events.idea: A silent film reel catches on a splice, repeating the same few frames. In one frame a hidden switch is visible behind the scenery.
events.why: The crew can use a flaw in the projection to find something concealed in the real room.

events.idea: A theremin-like tone rises as hands approach a locked case. Matching a short sequence of notes releases the latch, but loud mistakes attract a patrol.
events.why: The crew performs a spatial melody under pressure and can trade speed for stealth.

events.idea: An arc lamp keeps going dark as a scavenger steals pieces of its circuit. A stranded guide needs the lamp long enough to lead a group across the room.
events.why: Protecting or improvising the connection creates a small escort challenge with a visible deadline.
